notes: 3rd edition by Deloitte's count. Two Deloitte Research TMT reports, 'Mobile and Wireless Predictions 2004' (10 predictions) and 'Wire-line Predictions 2004' (10 predictions), both read in full from Internet Archive copies on deloitte.com/dtt/. Published date from the file name (dtt_tmt_WirelinePredictions_012704); PDF creation dates 21 and 22 January 2004. No Technology or Media predictions for 2004 were found: Wayback CDX for all PDFs under deloitte.com/dtt/ lists none, which fits Computerworld calling the 2005 Technology report Deloitte's first technology predictions. Rank is the printed number; it restarts per report (section).

entries.title: Voice will continue to dominate cellular mobile's revenues and profits.
entries.quote: Throughout 2004, all operators will continue to earn the majority of their revenues from voice services.
entries.metric: voice share of mobile operator revenues
entries.subject: Mobile voice revenue
entries.note: Deloitte Research TMT 'Mobile and Wireless Predictions 2004', read from the Internet Archive copy on deloitte.com/dtt/.

entries.title: Cellular mobile data growth will slow, dragged by stagnant consumer text messaging growth.
entries.quote: However SMS volumes will start to plateau in many countries, and based upon current projections, whilst WAP, internet browsing and MMS will all grow in 2004, their higher usage will not compensate for the anticipated deceleration in SMS growth.
entries.subject: SMS
entries.note: Deloitte Research TMT 'Mobile and Wireless Predictions 2004', read from the Internet Archive copy on deloitte.com/dtt/.

entries.title: Cellular mobile penetration rates will continue rising.
entries.quote: Despite the perennial cries that most mobile markets in developed countries are saturated, in 2004 the number of mobile subscribers will continue in all countries.
entries.subject: Mobile subscriber growth
entries.note: Deloitte Research TMT 'Mobile and Wireless Predictions 2004', read from the Internet Archive copy on deloitte.com/dtt/. Quote as printed (a word such as 'to grow' appears to be missing).

entries.title: More 3G, but not yet for the masses.
entries.quote: A further round of 3G networks will be launched commercially in 2004, although collectively these will only represent a minority of all operators.
entries.subject: 3G mobile networks
entries.note: Deloitte Research TMT 'Mobile and Wireless Predictions 2004', read from the Internet Archive copy on deloitte.com/dtt/.

entries.title: Mobilizing the enterprise will spread but remain niche.
entries.quote: A second round of enterprises and government departments will start to mobile enable their workers in 2004, focusing on field force workers.
entries.subject: Enterprise mobile applications
entries.note: Deloitte Research TMT 'Mobile and Wireless Predictions 2004', read from the Internet Archive copy on deloitte.com/dtt/.

entries.title: Push applications will be far more effective than pull applications for cellular mobile.
entries.quote: The most successful applications will be push applications, such as SMS, MMS (where this works) and push e-mail. Data applications such as WAP and mobile browsing will continue to under-perform both in term of usage and revenues.
entries.subject: Mobile data services
entries.note: Deloitte Research TMT 'Mobile and Wireless Predictions 2004', read from the Internet Archive copy on deloitte.com/dtt/.

entries.title: The mobile internet, as a major revenue stream, remains an aspiration.
entries.quote: Mobile phones will increasingly support Internet browsing, although this will remain a frustrating and expensive experience
entries.subject: Mobile internet
entries.note: Deloitte Research TMT 'Mobile and Wireless Predictions 2004', read from the Internet Archive copy on deloitte.com/dtt/.

entries.title: WiFi hot spots will remain more froth than substance.
entries.quote: Throughout 2004, the majority of WiFi hot spots will remain unused for the majority of the day.
entries.subject: Wi-Fi hotspots
entries.note: Deloitte Research TMT 'Mobile and Wireless Predictions 2004', read from the Internet Archive copy on deloitte.com/dtt/. Also: the majority of laptop PCs and PDAs in 2004 will not feature Wireless LAN.

entries.title: Wireless LAN will have most impact in non-office enterprise environments and homes.
entries.quote: The major growth for Wireless LAN, in terms of both number of deployments and volume of data carried, will be for private deployment in businesses and homes.
entries.subject: Wireless LAN
entries.note: Deloitte Research TMT 'Mobile and Wireless Predictions 2004', read from the Internet Archive copy on deloitte.com/dtt/.

entries.title: Colour and polyphony will enhance the mobile phone's personality and drive revenues.
entries.quote: By the end of 2004, the majority of handsets being shipped into developed countries will feature colour screens and polyphonic ring-tones.
entries.metric: share of handsets shipped into developed countries with colour screens and polyphonic ringtones
entries.subject: Colour-screen handsets
entries.note: Deloitte Research TMT 'Mobile and Wireless Predictions 2004', read from the Internet Archive copy on deloitte.com/dtt/.

entries.title: Steady broadband adoption.
entries.quote: By the end of the year broadband penetration rates will have exceeded 10% of population in only a dozen countries around the world.
entries.metric: countries with broadband penetration above 10% of population
entries.subject: Broadband adoption
entries.note: Deloitte Research TMT 'Wire-line Predictions 2004', read from the Internet Archive copy on deloitte.com/dtt/. Also: cellular penetration will exceed 90% in over ten countries by end 2004.

entries.title: The broadband appliance hits the High Street in Q4, 2004.
entries.quote: A range of broadband appliances will hit the shelves of major domestic electronics retailers for the 2004 holiday season.
entries.subject: Broadband appliances
entries.note: Deloitte Research TMT 'Wire-line Predictions 2004', read from the Internet Archive copy on deloitte.com/dtt/. The report adds that bestseller status 'may have to wait until 2006'.

entries.title: End-to-End VoIP is an essential element of operators' general strategy, even if usage in 2004 will be niche.
entries.quote: Voice over IP will remain a niche application for both business and residential customers in most countries.
entries.subject: VoIP
entries.note: Deloitte Research TMT 'Wire-line Predictions 2004', read from the Internet Archive copy on deloitte.com/dtt/.

entries.title: Data charging becomes variable, as price gets flatter.
entries.quote: Data is migrating from a pure all you-can eat-model to one based indirectly on usage
entries.subject: Broadband pricing
entries.note: Deloitte Research TMT 'Wire-line Predictions 2004', read from the Internet Archive copy on deloitte.com/dtt/.

entries.title: Wire-line still dominates voice.
entries.quote: In developed countries, the majority of minutes will still be carried over the fixed network in 2004.
entries.metric: share of voice minutes carried on fixed networks in developed countries
entries.subject: Fixed-line voice
entries.note: Deloitte Research TMT 'Wire-line Predictions 2004', read from the Internet Archive copy on deloitte.com/dtt/.

entries.title: WiFi hot spots will remain more froth than substance.
entries.quote: It is unlikely that operators (wire-line or cellular mobile) who have invested in WiFi hot spots will see much return on their investment in 2004.
entries.subject: Wi-Fi hotspots
entries.note: Deloitte Research TMT 'Wire-line Predictions 2004', read from the Internet Archive copy on deloitte.com/dtt/. Same headline as Mobile and Wireless prediction 8.

entries.title: Wireless LAN will have most impact in non-office enterprise environments and will drive demand for the core network.
entries.quote: Wireless LAN will cause most disruption where it allows a broadband network to reach where the wired LAN currently cannot reach
entries.subject: Wireless LAN
entries.note: Deloitte Research TMT 'Wire-line Predictions 2004', read from the Internet Archive copy on deloitte.com/dtt/.

entries.title: A wide range of competitors will continue to reduce incumbents' market share.
entries.quote: The emergence of carrier pre-selection will lead to continuing reductions in incumbents' market share of the residential market.
entries.subject: Telecom incumbent market share
entries.note: Deloitte Research TMT 'Wire-line Predictions 2004', read from the Internet Archive copy on deloitte.com/dtt/.

entries.title: Off shoring will offer a double opportunity for the fixed communications sector.
entries.quote: Deloitte Research estimates that some 2 million jobs in the financial sector alone will move off shore in the medium term.
entries.subject: Offshoring
entries.note: Deloitte Research TMT 'Wire-line Predictions 2004', read from the Internet Archive copy on deloitte.com/dtt/.

entries.title: Operators turn to technology for revenue growth.
entries.quote: Faced with growing competition and falling margin for core products, operators will increasingly develop new revenues streams based upon the provision of IT and networks solutions.
entries.subject: Telecom operator IT services
entries.note: Deloitte Research TMT 'Wire-line Predictions 2004', read from the Internet Archive copy on deloitte.com/dtt/.
